This game gripped me basically from the moment I opened it. I genuinely sat on the title screen for like two minutes before pressing anything because the art direction and music were that good. Probably the best first impression a game has ever given me.

The story kept me interested throughout and Verso was easily my favourite character. The combat took me a little while to get used to, but once it clicked it was sick. Having an RPG combat system mixed with dodges, parries and almost Naruto Storm-style quick-time events is such a good combination.

I also really liked how the levels were designed. They're linear enough that I always felt like I was progressing somewhere, without being Devil May Cry levels of "walk down this corridor and fight." It was a really nice middle ground.

I unfortunately had to stop playing for a while right after finishing Act 2 because of other commitments, which was probably the worst possible place to take a break. Act 2 almost feels like a resolution in itself, so I struggled to get back into Act 3 afterwards. Once I actually did though, I finished the rest of the game in about three days.

My biggest criticism is that the game somehow feels a little small despite having basically the perfect runtime. I finished it at around 30 hours and wouldn't really want the main story to be much longer. I just wish the world had more characters outside of the main cast who were properly developed, and I would have loved more combat options or some genuinely weird builds and abilities to play around with. By the end I was getting a little tired of running variations of Maelle, Verso and Sciel.

But those are pretty minor complaints compared to how much I enjoyed everything else. Incredible art direction, incredible music, a great story, fun combat and characters I actually cared about.

review:
[h1]NO SPOILERS - 7/10[/h1]

[hr][/hr]
[b]TL;DR[/b] - I played almost [b]100 hours[/b] in the span of a single week, defeated almost everything except the very last 3 super bosses in the Endless Tower. The game is really fun but the combat is unbalanced and broken, I don't think it deserved "Game of the year 2025" (a lot of hype), and it definitely did not deserve "Best Role Playing Game 2025" award.

[h3]Short version[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Pros:[/b] Amazing graphics (I also played with DLSS 5 and it looked like cinema), the story and acting are really good, they make you actually care for the characters. The combat is entertaining but has a huge RPG balancing flaw that was simply never fixed, I also had lots of fun making builds and whatnot ( [b][i]I highly suggest to not Google for builds, simply do them yourself[/i][/b] )

[*][b]Cons:[/b] There are a lot of areas that required "Quality of Life" updates that never happened, like a much better loadout system (skills, weapons, luminas), features for organizing pictos, lack of meaningful side quests, and most importantly the damage balance is just non-existent.

[*][b]Verdict:[/b] [b]7/10[/b], the game is really good and entertaining, however its most important RPG aspect which is combat is simply broken and was never fixed, it did not deserve "Best RPG 2025" award.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Long version[/h3]

The game performance was really good compared to what we have nowadays, I played with High settings and DLSS 5 balanced (Neural Rendering), I was playing at 80 FPS, which by comparison in other games under the same settings I was getting around 50 FPS.

Visually speaking, the environment and characters are out of this world, even more so when using DLSS 5 Neural Rendering, I spent a bunch of time taking screenshots as it looked completely astonishing.

The story and characters really captures you as a player, you can feel their fear, anguish, joy and sadness. It's among the few games that actually manage to transmit the character's feelings to the player, they did a perfect job on that.

However, the game was overly-hyped, in my opinion. I very much enjoyed the game up until half way through the story, at which point the game allowed me to finish every single encounter in 1 to 3 turns max (including bosses), and that went all the way through finishing the story. Then it only got more absurd after finishing the main story (one-shots).

Allow me to repeat, me, a player who did not use Google to search for builds, was allowed to [b][i]figuratively[/i][/b] one-shot his way through the main story at around half way through it, then [b][i]literally[/i][/b] one-shot post-story optional content and bosses, with the exception of the Super Bosses at Endless Tower and one or two bosses that took more than 3 turns.

The game went from a good pacing combat to just absolute nuts, the balancing is non-existent on this game, they did an awful job and combat is the base of RPGs, so how did they win the GOTY 2025? Scrap that, how did they even win the "Best RPG" award?

Bosses should take at least 10 minutes, not 10 seconds (I am not even joking).

So hype aside, it's a good game but far away from perfect, would recommend but it's not in my top 10 games.

One of the Best Gaming Experiences I've Ever Had!


This is actually my first ever review, and I couldn't think of a better game to write one for than Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.


Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of those rare games that makes you feel as though you're genuinely part of its world rather than simply playing through it. The immersion, atmosphere, and storytelling drew me in so completely that I found myself invested in every moment. As someone who usually dislikes cutscenes and tends to skip them whenever possible, watching every single cutscene in this game says more than enough about how deeply it captivated me.


The soundtrack deserves special recognition. I genuinely loved every song in the game, and the music plays an enormous role in making the experience so memorable. Combined with the incredible art direction, beautifully designed environments, and compelling characters, it creates an atmosphere that is difficult to put into words.


The gameplay was another major highlight for me. The ability to experiment with different builds, mix and match abilities, and develop unique strategies makes the combat incredibly engaging. The variety of encounters and the design of the bosses kept me invested throughout my journey. What surprised me most was how much I enjoyed the turn-based combat. The game almost feels like a turn-based Soulslike, combining strategic decision-making with challenging encounters and rewarding progression. It's a concept I hadn't fully appreciated before, but Expedition 33 has opened the door to an entirely new style of gameplay for me.


It's also one of the few games I've ever committed to completing 100%, earning every achievement along the way. The journey was certainly not without its frustrations, though. My biggest complaint is that completing every achievement requires a New Game+ playthrough. Having to go through another playthrough solely to finish the achievement list was disappointing, and I wish everything could have been completed in a single run. However, this is my only significant criticism, and it hardly diminishes the overall experience.


Everything else came together exceptionally well. From the world design and characters to the soundtrack, combat, bosses, and sheer atmosphere, Expedition 33 delivered an experience that genuinely resonated with me. It reminded me of what makes video games such a special medium: the ability to immerse yourself in another world, become invested in its journey, and walk away with an experience that stays with you long after the credits roll.


I know I'll remember this game for a long time. It has not only become one of my favourite games of all time, but has also changed my expectations of what a game can achieve when its different elements come together so beautifully.


For my first review, I couldn't have asked for a better game to write about. Thank you to the developers for creating such an unforgettable experience.

Review:
With its innovative use of light and shadow, Clair Obscur Expedition 33 redefines the adventure genre and creates an immersive, intriguing, and alive world. This expedition is more than simply a trek; it's an artistic masterwork that combines cutting-edge gameplay mechanics with powerful visual storytelling, with each scene acting like a living chiaroscuro painting. Expedition 33's flawless blend of narrative complexity and perceptually challenging environmental challenges is what makes it genuinely exceptional and worthy of game-of-the-year honors. By changing light sources, players must navigate through shifting shadows and uncover hidden facts, transforming the idea of exploration into a unique sensory and intellectual experience. Clair Obscur Expedition 33's soundtrack creates an enthralling soundscape that draws you farther into the enigmatic universe of the game, making it incredibly addicting. The soundtrack's eerie melodies and ethereal tones enhance the emotional intensity at every step by flawlessly balancing the interaction of light and shade.

✅ Good
-Stunning Visuals
-Innovative Gameplay
-Addictive Soundtrack

❌ Bad
-Slow pacing

I've attatched my PC Spces - its not a budget build or something. 

Despite the issues I still recommend it.

[spoiler] There is also a narrative choice I hate in this game - the entire world the game takes place in is revealed to be canonically fictional... like an "...and it was all a dream" ending. Really sucks out the emotional weight the game had when it started. [/spoiler]

✅ Pros: Emotionally gripping narrative with deep themes, innovative turn-based combat with real-time parry/dodge mechanics, breathtaking Surrealist & Belle Époque art direction, phenomenal soundtrack and top-tier voice acting.
❌ Cons: Strict combat timing requirements can feel exhausting for some, linear world exploration with limited traversal options, lack of a minimap and minor visual lip-sync bugs.

I almost didnt like it. It felt like the fight mechanics were kinda lame. Like stun was a 5 turn build up just to have it wear off after a turn most of the time, Lune and Gustave felt similar. Sciel was a mid range option with ons and offs of high dps, Verso was even worse than everyone else as he lost progression as he took damage and the move sets for all the enemies were so varied that it made it really hard to maintain a decent rank. MONOCO was the most fun for me to play. Collecting moves from downed enemies was a rather novel mechanic and gave him a more readily available skill tree. Maelle was my most consistent damage doer but even she would struggle to get her moves off the ground sometime. Yes I played on easy as this game was already out of the spot light when I mostly played it for the story which didnt make sense for the first 8/10ths of the game. That was annoying. A story driven game like this should have a more clear story at the beginning. I do like dramatic reveals and unreliable witness based perspectives but I had no motivation to fight past the vagueness of the depressing story. By the way SF... That first epilogue was not an epilogue! 1 Epilogues take place after the main game and are story exits for every character usually. 2 You cant have an epilogue after an epilogue. That just proves that the first one was not an epilogue. 3 If understanding your whole game only happens in the epilogue then you will have discouraged most of your gamers from finishing the game and truly appreciating what occured in the main story. For me, your game only really happened in the first epilogue. which is not how epilogues work. I almost just put down the game at the 10 hour mark and said, 'nope, its a random depressing story that is beautifully rendered but ultimately pointless. dont buy.' BUT! because of how it ended, (and I think I picked the better ending,) it ended up being a powerful story about dealing with grief and loss and the effect of a loss on everyone it touches. For me it ended well, but sucked the life out of me up until that point. Maybe that was the point... or maybe I was just bored on easy mode. 7/10. Could done this with less fighting.
